issues.description: The solution implementation of Lecture.java declares attributes using snake_case names (e.g. number_of_guest_students) but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods use camelCase names (e.g. numberOfGuestStudents, lectureName). This name mismatch is an internal structural inconsistency in the solution repository that will cause compilation errors and confuse students who compare the solution to the UML/problem statement. The problem statement and UML use camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), so the solution should use the same names consistently.
issues.suggested_fix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and the rest of the code. Rename the declared fields in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Alternatively, change all usages in constructor/methods to refer to the declared snake_case fields—but the recommended fix is to adopt the camelCase names from the problem statement/UML so the solution, template expectations, and documentation all align.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML + tasks) specifies attributes using camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares the same conceptual attributes using snake_case field names (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while its constructor and methods use camelCase names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This creates a naming mismatch across artifacts and an internal inconsistency in the solution (fields vs. used identifiers). Students comparing the UML to the reference solution may be confused about the correct attribute names to implement and how constructor/method identifiers map to fields; the inconsistency also appears to be an unintentional oversight (and would cause compilation/clarity issues in the reference).
issues.suggested_fix: Make identifier names consistent with the problem UML and Java conventions. Rename the solution's fields to the camelCase names used in the problem (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and ensure the constructor, getters, setters and other methods consistently reference those field names. Alternatively, if snake_case is intentionally preferred, update the problem/UML to use the same names — but prefer camelCase to match Java naming conventions and the exercise description.
